verdict: Mondelez's GAAP profit jumped 76% to $1.3B — mostly because cocoa and currency hedge accounting swung in its favor this year; the underlying snack business grew a steadier 2%.

oneTimers: Gross profit includes a large favorable swing in mark-to-market accounting on cocoa and currency derivatives — the same mechanism depressed last year's quarter (gross margin was 26.8% then, 39.4% now). Adjusted results strip these swings out, which is why adjusted EPS grew only 5.5% at constant currency while GAAP EPS rose 79%.

takeaways.title: The margin jump is accounting, not pricing power
takeaways.text: Gross margin leapt from 26.8% to 39.4% almost entirely on mark-to-market swings in cocoa and currency hedges. The underlying (adjusted) gross profit grew much more modestly.

takeaways.title: Steady underlying growth
takeaways.text: Organic revenue rose 2.1%: selling slightly more snacks (volume/mix +1.8 points) with near-flat pricing (+0.3 points) after last year's big chocolate price rises.

takeaways.title: Europe is the soft spot
takeaways.text: European organic sales fell 2.1% — shoppers pushed back on chocolate prices (pricing subtracted 3.7 points there) — while emerging markets grew 4.1% organically.

footerNote: Net earnings of $1,305M are attributable to Mondelez; consolidated net earnings were $1,308M. Equity-method investments (including its stake in JDE Peet's) contributed $11M of earnings, shown net of the $3M belonging to noncontrolling interests.
